# bootstrap-ingest (agent prose)

You are reading a SUPPLIED prior bootstrap to load prior session state.
You do NOT scan directories. The bootstrap-start macro resolved the
selection (operator-driven, Section B.3) and handed you an absolute
`prior_bootstrap_path`. You produce a synthesized briefing — never a
verbatim YAML dump.

## Steps

1. Load the supplied `prior_bootstrap_path`. If the file does not exist
   OR cannot be opened, raise BROKEN_BOOTSTRAP and dispatch to recovery.
2. Parse the YAML. If parse fails (Q7 condition 1), raise BROKEN_BOOTSTRAP
   and dispatch to recovery, capturing the parse error and partial raw
   text for R3.
3. Verify required top-level keys: `project`, `session`, `tasks`,
   `environment`, `context_file_audit`. (Note: `decisions` is no longer
   required; it is allowed but session-scoped.) If any required key is
   missing (Q7 condition 2), raise BROKEN_BOOTSTRAP and dispatch to
   recovery.
4. Run data integrity checks: session.id matches filename timestamp,
   all task ids unique within session, all referenced session_origins
   are non-empty strings. If any integrity check fails (Q7 condition 3),
   raise BROKEN_BOOTSTRAP and dispatch to recovery.
5. Compute counts: ACTIVE/BLOCKED/DEFERRED tasks, decisions, open issues,
   stale audit entries.
6. Compose synthesized briefing per output contract. Do NOT dump YAML at
   the user. Do NOT paraphrase content beyond what the contract requires.
   Include `next_session_kickoff` in the output contract as a verbatim
   copy of `parsed_bootstrap.next_session_kickoff` when that key exists;
   otherwise null.
7. Hand off the parsed bootstrap object to `bootstrap-audit`.

## Recovery flow (dispatched by step 1, 2, 3, or 4 OR by start macro
## when stale-lock-with-missing-bootstrap detected)

- **R3 review partial.** If a partial broken file exists, read as raw
  text, extract recoverable sections (top-of-file identity block usually
  intact). Carry findings forward to R5.
- **R5 live-dir recovery.** While archive housekeeping is deferred, review
  loose canonical bootstraps in
  `{project_root}/02_working/chat-sessions/bootstrap/`. Exclude the broken
  bootstrap file and supplemental derivatives unless the operator explicitly
  selects a supplemental. Prefer the most recent valid canonical bootstrap
  by filename timestamp, then internal `session.ended`, then file modified
  time only if needed. Review in entirety. Perform 360 review using all
  available live-dir bootstraps. Generate line-by-line status report on
  the previous bootstrap's open items. Generate a supplemental bootstrap
  named `{ProjectName}_{BrokenSessionID}S.yaml` in the live dir, with
  `supplemental: true` and `supersedes: <broken_session_id>`.
- **R6 broken-file disposal.** AFTER supplemental is written and verified
  (validate_bootstrap.py --finalized passes), send the broken original
  to the OS desktop recycle bin per
  `C:/Users/rtoth/.cursor/commands/housekeeping/command.housekeeping.yaml`
  `removal_flow`. NEVER use Remove-Item. Recoverable from recycle bin if
  review surfaces forensic need.
- **No valid recovery candidate fallback (Q6).** If the live directory has
  no usable recovery candidate, ask the operator whether to start
  session-zero using the already-known `project_root` and `project_name`.
  Only explicit YES signals session-zero to bootstrap-init. No carry-forward.

After recovery generates the supplemental, re-enter step 1 with
`prior_bootstrap_path = <supplemental_path>`.

## Hard rules

- Never substitute agent memory for the actual file content.
- Never dump YAML in chat as a substitute for synthesis.
- Never proceed to project work — that requires audit + init to complete first.
- Never emit "I will now read the bootstrap" or any preamble. The first
  visible token is the populated output contract.
- Never scan directories to pick a bootstrap. Selection is the start
  macro's job.
- Never silently fix a broken bootstrap in place. Recovery is the only path.
- Never delete the broken file with Remove-Item. R6 recycle-bin only.
